from `keystone-dashboard-layout-vue`'s own main entry point — nothing
extra to install or configure for full TypeScript support.

## Components

`GridLayout`, `GridItem`, `CustomCloseButton`, `CustomDragElement` — see
[Components](/vue/components/) for full documentation.

Their prop types (`IGridLayoutProps`, `IGridItemProps`,
`ICustomCloseButtonProps`, `ICustomDragElementProps`) are also directly
importable — useful for typing a wrapper component's own props, or a
`ref<InstanceType<typeof GridItem>>()`:

```ts
import type { IGridLayoutProps, IGridItemProps } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-vue';
```

Each prop's own meaning is documented on [GridLayout props](/vue/components/grid-layout/props/)
and [GridItem props](/vue/components/grid-item/props/) — not repeated
here as a second, separately-maintained table.

## Interfaces

| Interface | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Eventbus (IEventsData)](/vue/api/interfaces/eventbus/) | The internal eventBus's drag/resize payload shape |
| [Layout (ILayoutItem, ILayoutItemRequired, TLayoutItem)](/vue/api/interfaces/layout/) | One entry in a `GridLayout`'s `layout` array |
| [ARIA labels (IGridAriaLabels)](/vue/api/interfaces/aria-labels/) | Localizable UI/ARIA strings, plus the exported `DEFAULT_ARIA_LABELS` constant |
| [Pluggable compaction (ICompactor)](/vue/api/interfaces/compactor/) | The `compactor` prop's interface, its context object, and the five built-in strategies |

## Drag & resize

- **Drag anywhere, or from a handle.** Every item is draggable by default; restrict it to a specific handle with `dragAllowFrom`, or exclude specific elements with `dragIgnoreFrom`. See [Drag allow/ignore elements](/vue/examples/drag-allow-ignore-elements/) and [Custom drag handle](/vue/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/).
- **Resize from any edge or corner** — top, right, bottom, left, and the diagonals — with optional `preserveAspectRatio` locking.
- **Min/max size constraints** (`minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`) per item.
- **Bounded dragging** — keep items from being dragged outside the container. See [Bounded drag](/vue/examples/bounded-drag/).
- **Static items** — lock specific items in place; they ignore dragging/resizing entirely and act as fixed obstacles for compaction. See [Static items](/vue/examples/static-items/).
- **Per-item `zIndex` override** — pin one item permanently above every other, including while others are mid-resize, regardless of the library's own implicit static/resizing stacking rules.
- **A separate header region** (`#header` slot) — an optional header area above an item's own main content, its own scrollable region taking whatever space remains.
- **Per-item `autoHeight`** — a live-resyncing height, driven by a real `ResizeObserver` on the item's own content rather than a one-time measurement. See [Per-item autoHeight](/vue/examples/per-item-auto-height/).

## Layout & collision

- **Automatic compaction.** Items fill gaps vertically by default; other items automatically move out of the way of a drag/resize.
- **Pluggable compaction strategy** (`compactType`) — five built-in strategies (vertical, horizontal, none, and overlap variants of each), or replace the algorithm entirely with a custom `ICompactor`. See [Pluggable compaction](/vue/examples/pluggable-compaction/).
- **Horizontal shift mode** — push colliding items left/right instead of down. See [Horizontal shift](/vue/examples/horizontal-shift/).
- **Prevent collision mode** — block a drag/resize instead of pushing other items, with a `MOVE_BLOCKED_BY_COLLISION` event so a consumer can give feedback the moment that happens. See [Prevent collision](/vue/examples/prevent-collision/) and [Blocked-move feedback](/vue/examples/blocked-move-feedback/).
- **Magnetic snap-to-grid** (`snapToGrid`/`snapThreshold`) — actually adjusts an item's landing position to align with a neighbor, not just a visual guide. See [Snap to grid](/vue/examples/snap-to-grid/).
- **Alignment guides** — Figma-style guide lines while dragging or resizing, wherever an item's edges line up with another's. See [Alignment guides while dragging](/vue/examples/alignment-guides/).
- **`restoreOnDrag`** — keep other items from compacting past their pre-drag position while a drag is in progress. See [Layout bounds & rendering options](/vue/examples/layout-bounds-rendering-options/).
- **Auto-sizing container** — the grid's height grows/shrinks to fit its content by default (`autoSize`, or the newer `heightMode` prop for finer control including `'scroll'`/`'fit'` modes). See [Auto-size grid on content](/vue/examples/auto-size-grid/).
- **Spacing indicators** — a labeled distance badge (e.g. "2 cols") in the gap between the active item and its nearest neighbor on each side (`showSpacingGuides`), independently toggleable alongside alignment guides.
- **Serializable layout.** The `layout` array is a plain, JSON-serializable structure you own — persist it anywhere. See [v-model & save/load layout](/vue/examples/save-load-layout/).
- **Named layout presets** (`useLayoutPresets`) — save and switch between multiple named arrangements, layered on the same serialize/restore primitives. See [Named layout presets](/vue/examples/named-presets/).
- **Grid-to-SVG export** (`exportLayoutAsSvg`) — a dependency-free utility producing a standalone SVG snapshot of the current layout. See [Export layout as SVG](/vue/examples/svg-export/).
- **Undo/redo** (`enableUndoRedo`, capped via `undoHistoryLimit`) — opt-in history at committed-change granularity (drag/resize end, add/remove), not per intermediate frame. See [Undo/redo](/vue/examples/undo-redo/).
- **Add/remove items freely**, with automatic re-compaction — no manual position math required. See [Add or remove items](/vue/examples/add-remove-items/).

## Multi-select & group operations

- **Select multiple items** — click to select, Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+click to add additively, click empty background to clear.
- **Group move and resize** — drag or resize any selected item and the rest of the selection moves or resizes by the same delta, from mouse or keyboard alike. See [Multi-select & group move/resize](/vue/examples/multi-select-group-move-resize/).

## Responsive

- **Breakpoint-based column counts**, with sensible defaults (`xxl`/`xl`/`lg`/`md`/`sm`/`xs`/`xxs`) and fully customizable breakpoints/columns. See [Responsive breakpoints](/vue/examples/responsive-breakpoints/).
- **Pre-defined layouts per breakpoint**, for full control over how content reflows instead of relying on auto-generation. See [Responsive predefined layouts](/vue/examples/responsive-predefined-layouts/).

## Internationalization

- **RTL mirroring** for an entire layout or individual items — positions (and dragging) flip horizontally with a single prop. See [Mirrored (RTL)](/vue/examples/mirrored-rtl/).

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard move & resize.** Every non-static, editable item is keyboard-focusable — arrow keys move it, Shift+arrow keys resize it — without needing any extra configuration. Reuses the exact same events/collision handling the mouse-driven path uses. See [Accessibility scope](/vue/guide/project/accessibility/) for the full scope, including what's deliberately not (yet) covered.
- **Screen reader support** — interactive items are announced with `role="group"` and a description of the available keyboard controls; visible focus indicator for keyboard users.
- **Localizable ARIA strings** (`ariaLabels`) — the close button's label, `aria-roledescription`, and the keyboard move/resize instructions are overridable (`GridLayout` grid-wide default, `GridItem` per-item override), rather than hardcoded English literals. See [Localizable ARIA strings](/vue/examples/aria-labels/).

## Cross-grid & external drag-and-drop

- **Drag items from outside the grid** using the browser's native HTML5 drag-and-drop API. See [Drag, drop from outside](/vue/examples/outside-drag-drop/).
- **Drag items between two independent grids.** See [Drag, drop from grid to grid](/vue/examples/cross-grid-drag-drop/).
- **Multiple grids on one page** with zero shared state or configuration. See [Multiple grids](/vue/examples/multiple-grids/).

## Styling & customization

- **Unstyled-by-default content** — `GridItem`'s slot holds whatever you put there; the library only handles position/size.
- **Built-in close button**, or bring your own via the exported `CustomCloseButton`/`CustomDragElement` components. See [Show close button](/vue/examples/close-button/) and [Custom drag handle & close button](/vue/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/).
- **Configurable border radius** per item. See [Border radius](/vue/examples/border-radius/).
- **Optional grid line guides**, useful while building a layout or as a permanent visual aid. See [Show grid lines](/vue/examples/grid-lines/).
- **CSS custom properties and SCSS variables** for deeper theming — see [Styling → Variables](/vue/components/styling/css-variables/).

## Developer experience

- **Full TypeScript support.** Every prop, event, enum, and interface is typed and exported from the package's main entry point — see [API](/vue/api/).
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** The drag/resize engine is built on native Pointer Events, not a third-party library — no `interact.js` or equivalent to audit or update.
- **A separate, framework-agnostic core entry point** exposing this library's own grid-layout math (collision detection, movement, compaction, and more) with zero Vue dependency and no live-DOM requirement — usable standalone, e.g. for server-side layout validation.
- **Vue 3 Composition API**, built with `<script setup>` throughout — works equally well with the Options API in consuming projects.
- **Well-tested.** A full unit, component, and end-to-end test suite backs every release, enforced in CI.
- **An editable playground on every example.** "Open in StackBlitz" opens a real, running project seeded from that exact example's own source, in a new tab — not a read-only code snippet.
GridLayoutComponent and GridItemComponent — the two standalone components this package exports.

The package exports these from its main entry point — both are
**standalone components**, added directly to your own component's
`imports` array, no `NgModule` required:

| Component | Selector | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [`GridLayoutComponent`](/angular/components/grid-layout/props/) | `kdl-grid-layout` | The grid container — owns the layout array, breakpoints, and collision/compaction logic. A fully controlled component (`layout` `@Input()` + `layoutChange` `@Output()`). |
| [`GridItemComponent`](/angular/components/grid-item/props/) | `kdl-grid-item` | A single draggable/resizable cell, projected as content of `GridLayoutComponent`. |

See [Styling](/angular/components/styling/) for the CSS custom
properties and class names used throughout.

```ts
import { GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-angular';
```

There's no default export — always import by name. See
[Installation](/angular/guide/installation/) if you haven't added the
package yet.

This package also has real, exported close-button and drag-handle
components, matching Vue and React — but note that `GridItemComponent`'s
own built-in close button (`showCloseButton` + a `removeItem`
`@Output()` you handle yourself) is a separate, simpler path most
consumers should reach for first; the standalone components below are
for a consumer who wants the same building blocks rendered somewhere
else entirely (e.g. inside a custom header). Any part of a
`GridItemComponent` is already a drag handle by default — restrict it
via `dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom` directly on `GridItemComponent`,
without needing the standalone drag-handle component below at all,
unless you want its specific rendered widget.

## Standalone utility components

Two additional standalone components exist for a consumer who wants
the same close-button/drag-handle *building blocks* Vue's own
`CustomCloseButton.vue`/`CustomDragElement.vue` provide, used outside
`GridItemComponent`'s own built-in rendering entirely — e.g. placed
inside a custom header region (see `GridItemHeaderDirective` above).
Neither is used internally by `GridLayoutComponent`/`GridItemComponent`
themselves; a consumer opts into either explicitly.

| Component | Selector | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [`GridItemCloseButtonComponent`](/angular/components/custom-close-button/) | `kdl-custom-close-button` | A standalone close button. Takes a required `i` — the id of whichever item it should remove — and emits `removeGridItem` with that id on click; wire that output to your own removal logic. |
| [`GridItemDragHandleComponent`](/angular/components/custom-drag-element/) | `kdl-custom-drag-element` | A standalone drag-handle widget (a labeled button plus a separate `.kdl-draggable-handle` hit-area — target that class, not the button itself, with `dragAllowFrom`). Takes an optional `text` input (default `'x'`) for the button's own label. |

```ts
import { GridItemCloseButtonComponent, GridItemDragHandleComponent } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-angular';
```

## A real, notable difference from React

Unlike the React package (where `GridItem` only takes `i`, reading
everything else — position, size, `isDraggable`, and so on — off the
matching entry in `GridLayout`'s own `layout` array), `GridItemComponent`
here takes `i`/`x`/`y`/`w`/`h` as its **own, direct, required
`@Input()`s** — the same shape Vue's `GridItem` uses. You bind each one
explicitly per item in your own template's `@for` loop; this component
doesn't read them off `layout` automatically.

## The imperative API

`GridLayoutComponent` also exposes public methods, reached via a
template reference variable (`#grid` + `@ViewChild` in your own
component, or a plain template variable for a direct template call) —
`compactNow()`/`rearrange()`, `duplicateItem(id)`, `undo()`/`redo()`
(plus the `canUndo`/`canRedo` public fields), `selectItem()`/
`deselectItem()`/`toggleItemSelection()`/`clearSelection()`,
`alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)`, `exportLayoutAsSvg()`,
and `scrollToItem(id)`/`focusItem(id)` — the Angular equivalent of
Vue's own `defineExpose`'d template-ref methods, or React's `ref`-based
imperative handle. See [Public members](/angular/api/interfaces/public-members/)
for the full reference.

## What this package exports

```ts
import {
  GridLayoutComponent,
  GridItemComponent,
  GridItemHeaderDirective,
  GridLayoutStorageService,
  GridLayoutPresetsService,
  GridItemDragHandleComponent,
```

That's the complete list. Unlike the Vue package, this package doesn't
re-export layout-data types, enums, or compaction/ARIA interfaces
through its own barrel either — those come from the shared
`keystone-dashboard-layout-core` package directly instead (see
below). There's also no separate exported type for the
`@Input()`/`@Output()` shapes the way React exports `IGridLayoutProps`/
`IGridItemProps` — an Angular `@Component`'s own class already **is**
its prop contract; there's no separate props-interface convention to
mirror here.

`GridItemHeaderDirective`, `GridLayoutStorageService`,
`GridLayoutPresetsService`, `GridItemDragHandleComponent`, and
`GridItemCloseButtonComponent` were fully implemented in the package's
own source but weren't actually exported from this barrel until a
recent fix — meaning no consumer could previously import any of these
five from `keystone-dashboard-layout-angular` at all, despite the
package's own `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` already describing them as
finished, public API. Confirm you're on a version that includes the
fix before relying on these five specifically.
:::

Draggable, resizable dashboard grid layout for Vue 3. Drag-and-drop widgets, responsive breakpoints, undo/redo, and zero runtime dependencies — a modern alternative to vue-grid-layout and grid-layout-plus.

**Keystone Dashboard Layout for Vue** is a draggable, resizable
dashboard grid component for Vue 3, built on the Composition API. If
you're building a customizable analytics dashboard, a widget-based
admin panel, a BI tool, or any screen where users rearrange their own
content by dragging and resizing panels, this is the grid-layout engine
underneath it — drag, resize from any of 8 edges/corners, multi-select
with group move/resize, undo/redo, and breakpoint-aware responsive
layouts, all with zero runtime dependencies.

```sh
npm i keystone-dashboard-layout-vue
```

## Why teams pick this over `vue-grid-layout`

The most well-known Vue grid-layout library, `vue-grid-layout`, has
never shipped an official Vue 3 release — years after Vue 3 became the
default. What filled that gap is a handful of independently maintained
community forks (`grid-layout-plus` chief among them), each roughly
matching the original's own feature set rather than extending it. This
library is a ground-up Vue 3 implementation with a materially larger
feature set: cross-grid drag-and-drop between independent grid
instances, magnetic snap-to-grid, visual alignment guides, named
layout presets, grid-to-SVG export, localizable ARIA strings, and
undo/redo — none of which any Vue grid-layout alternative currently
offers. See [Comparison: alternatives](/vue/guide/project/comparison-alternatives/)
for the full, honestly-scored feature table.

## A quick look

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { GridLayout, GridItem } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-vue';
import type { TLayout } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-core';

const layout = ref<TLayout>([
  { i: 'a', x: 0, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
  { i: 'b', x: 2, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
]);
</script>

<template>
  <GridLayout v-model:layout="layout">
    <GridItem v-for="item in layout" :key="item.i" :i="item.i">
      Panel {{ item.i }}
    </GridItem>
  </GridLayout>
</template>
```

That's a working, draggable, resizable, responsive dashboard grid — no
manual position math, no separate drag library to wire up.

## Drag & resize

- **Drag anywhere, or from a handle.** Every item is draggable by default; restrict it to a specific handle with `dragAllowFrom`, or exclude specific elements with `dragIgnoreFrom` (and `resizeIgnoreFrom` for resize specifically). See [Drag allow/ignore elements](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/05-drag-allow-ignore-elements) and [Custom drag handle](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/18-custom-drag-handle-close-button).
- **Resize from any edge or corner** — top, right, bottom, left, and the diagonals — with optional `preserveAspectRatio` locking. See [Size constraints & aspect ratio](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/38-size-constraints-aspect-ratio), [Restricting resize handles to specific edges](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/52-restrict-resize-handles), and [Resize direction toggles](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/53-resize-direction-toggles).
- **Min/max size constraints** (`minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`) per item. See [Size constraints & aspect ratio](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/38-size-constraints-aspect-ratio).
- **Bounded dragging** (`isBounded`) — keep items from being dragged outside the container. See [Bounded drag](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/02-bounded-drag).
- **Static items** — lock specific items in place; they ignore dragging/resizing entirely and act as fixed obstacles for compaction. See [Static items](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/17-static-items).
- **Per-item `zIndex` override** — pin one item permanently above every other, including while others are mid-resize, regardless of the library's own implicit static/resizing stacking rules. See [Per-item zIndex override](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/49-per-item-z-index).
- **A separate header region** — a `GridItemHeaderDirective` marker directive (`[kdlGridItemHeader]`) applied to your own header content, projected into `GridItemComponent`'s own dedicated header region instead of its plain default content. Angular's equivalent of Vue's named slot or React's `header` render prop, expressed as a queryable content-projection marker instead. See [Custom header](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/48-custom-header-slot).
- **Per-item `autoHeight`** — a live-resyncing height, driven by a real `ResizeObserver` on the item's own content rather than a one-time measurement. See [Per-item autoHeight](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/31-per-item-auto-height).
- **`dragActivationDistance`** — a per-pointer-type drag-start threshold, so a small accidental movement doesn't immediately start a drag. See [Drag activation distance](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/51-drag-activation-distance).

## Layout & collision

- **Automatic compaction.** Items fill gaps vertically by default; other items automatically move out of the way of a drag/resize.
- **Pluggable compaction strategy** (`compactType`) — five built-in strategies (vertical, horizontal, none, and overlap variants of each), or replace the algorithm entirely with a custom `compactor` `@Input()`. See [Pluggable compaction](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/42-pluggable-compaction).
- **Horizontal shift mode** (`horizontalShift`) — push colliding items left/right instead of down. See [Horizontal shift](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/15-horizontal-shift).
- **Prevent collision mode** (`preventCollision`) — block a drag/resize instead of pushing other items, with a `moveBlockedByCollision` `@Output()` so a consumer can give feedback the moment that happens. See [Prevent collision](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/08-prevent-collision) and [Blocked-move feedback](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/30-blocked-move-feedback).
- **Magnetic snap-to-grid** (`snapToGrid`/`snapThreshold`) — actually adjusts an item's landing position to align with a neighbor, not just a visual guide. See [Snap to grid](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/32-snap-to-grid).
- **Alignment guides** (`showAlignmentGuides`) — Figma-style guide lines while dragging or resizing, wherever an item's edges line up with another's. See [Alignment guides while dragging](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/26-alignment-guides).
- **`restoreOnDrag`** — keep other items from compacting past their pre-drag position while a drag is in progress. See [Layout bounds & rendering options](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/41-layout-bounds-rendering-options).
- **Auto-sizing container** — the grid's height grows/shrinks to fit its content by default (`autoSize`, or the newer `heightMode` `@Input()` for finer control including `'scroll'`/`'fit'` modes). See [Auto-size grid on content](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/20-auto-size-grid) and [Height modes](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/50-height-modes).
- **Spacing indicators** (`showSpacingGuides`) — a labeled distance badge (e.g. "2 cols") in the gap between the active item and its nearest neighbor on each side, independently toggleable alongside alignment guides. See [Spacing indicators](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/47-spacing-indicators).
- **Serializable layout.** The `layout` array is a plain, JSON-serializable structure you own — persist it anywhere. See [Save/load layout](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/19-save-load-layout).
- **Named layout presets** (`GridLayoutPresetsService`) — save and switch between multiple named arrangements, layered on the same serialize/restore primitives `GridLayoutStorageService` uses. See [Named layout presets](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/35-named-presets).
- **Grid-to-SVG export** (`exportLayoutAsSvg()`, a public method on `GridLayoutComponent`) — a dependency-free utility producing a standalone SVG snapshot of the current layout. See [Export layout as SVG](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/28-svg-export).
- **Undo/redo** (`enableUndoRedo`, capped via `undoHistoryLimit`) — opt-in history at committed-change granularity (drag/resize end, add/remove), not per intermediate frame. Reach `undo()`/`redo()` and the `canUndo`/`canRedo` flags via a template reference variable on `GridLayoutComponent`. See [Undo/redo](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/43-undo-redo).
- **Add/remove items freely**, with automatic re-compaction — no manual position math required. `duplicateItem(id)` (also a public method) clones an existing item into a collision-safe spot below it. See [Add or remove items](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/10-add-remove-items) and [compactNow, rearrange & duplicateItem](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/29-compact-now-rearrange-duplicate-item).
- **`distributeEvenly`** — spreads an out-of-bounds item to the next available slot on a responsive breakpoint change, instead of clamping it to the right edge.
- **Programmatic grid dimensions** and **live layout lifecycle events** (`layoutReady` plus the granular drag `@Output()`s) for observing exactly when the grid settles or an interaction completes. See [Grid dimensions](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/44-grid-dimensions) and [Layout lifecycle events](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/40-layout-lifecycle-events).
- **Switching layouts**, including forcing a full remount when Angular's own `@if`/`track` change is the simplest way to reset internal state. See [Switching layouts & forcing a remount](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/45-switching-layouts-remount).

## Multi-select & group operations

- **Select multiple items** (`multiSelect`) — click to select, Ctrl/Cmd+click to add additively, click empty background to clear, and **Shift-click to select a contiguous range** from the last-clicked anchor. See [Multi-select & group move/resize](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/37-multi-select-group-move-resize).
- **Group move and resize** — drag or resize any selected item and the rest of the selection moves or resizes by the same delta, from mouse or keyboard alike. See [Multi-select & group move/resize](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/37-multi-select-group-move-resize).
- **Align/distribute commands** (`alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)`, public methods on `GridLayoutComponent`) — align a selection to an edge, or evenly space what's between. See [Align & distribute selected items](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/46-align-distribute-selected).

## Responsive

- **Breakpoint-based column counts**, with sensible defaults and fully customizable `breakpoints`/`cols`. See [Responsive breakpoints](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/07-responsive-breakpoints).
- **Pre-defined layouts per breakpoint** (`responsiveLayouts`), for full control over how content reflows instead of relying on auto-generation. See [Responsive predefined layouts](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/09-responsive-predefined-layouts).

## Internationalization

- **RTL mirroring** (`isMirrored`) for an entire layout or individual items — positions (and dragging) flip horizontally with a single `@Input()`. The resize-specific edge-swap math for RTL is a direct analogy to the LTR case rather than exhaustively verified against a real browser — the same "best-effort" caveat this package's own source carries for that one corner. See [Mirrored (RTL)](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/06-mirrored-rtl).

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard move & resize.** Every non-static, editable item is keyboard-focusable — arrow keys move it, Shift+arrow keys resize it — without needing any extra configuration, including RTL-aware key direction and `multiSelect` group-move/resize engagement. See [Accessibility scope](/angular/guide/project/accessibility/) once that page lands, for the full scope, including what's deliberately not (yet) covered.
- **Screen reader support** — interactive items are announced with an item-role description and a description of the available keyboard controls; visible focus indicator for keyboard users.
- **Localizable ARIA strings** (`ariaLabels`) — the close button's label, role description, and the keyboard move/resize instructions are overridable (`GridLayoutComponent` grid-wide default, `GridItemComponent` per-item override), rather than hardcoded English literals. See [Localizable ARIA strings](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/36-aria-labels).

## Cross-grid & external drag-and-drop

- **Drag items from outside the grid** (`allowOutsideDrop`) using the browser's native HTML5 drag-and-drop API, with a live drop-position placeholder while dragging over the grid. See [Drag, drop from outside](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/11-outside-drag-drop) and [outsideDropAccept & readOutsideDropPayload](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/34-outside-drop-accept-payload).
- **Drag items between two independent grids** (`allowCrossGridDrag`/`disableExternalDrop`/`layoutId`) via a real first-fit bin-pack, not a naive placement then compaction sorts out. See [Drag, drop from grid to grid](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/12-cross-grid-drag-drop) and [Cross-grid drop restrictions](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/22-cross-grid-drop-restrictions).
- **Multiple grids on one page** with zero shared state — each `GridLayoutComponent` provides its own, independent `GridEventBusService` instance — beyond an optional `layoutId`. See [Multiple grids](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/04-multiple-grids) and [Drag, drop from outside into multiple grids](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/23-outside-drag-drop-multiple-grids).

## Styling & customization

- **Unstyled-by-default content** — `GridItemComponent`'s projected content holds whatever you put there; the library only handles position/size.
- **Built-in close button** (`showCloseButton` + a `removeItem` `@Output()` you handle yourself), and any part of an item is a drag handle by default, restrictable via `dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom`. Standalone [`GridItemCloseButtonComponent`](/angular/components/custom-close-button/)/[`GridItemDragHandleComponent`](/angular/components/custom-drag-element/) also exist for the same building blocks used outside `GridItemComponent`'s own rendering entirely (e.g. inside a custom header). See [Show close button](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/13-close-button) and [Custom drag handle & close button](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/18-custom-drag-handle-close-button).
- **Configurable border radius** per item (`borderRadiusPx`/`useBorderRadius`, grid-wide default + per-item override). See [Border radius](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/14-border-radius).
- **Optional grid line guides** (`showGridLines`), useful while building a layout or as a permanent visual aid. See [Show grid lines](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/16-grid-lines).
- **Configurable transition duration/easing** (`transitionDurationMs`/`transitionTimingFunction`), applied via CSS custom properties. See [Configurable transition duration & easing](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/24-transition-duration-easing).
- **Configurable resize-hint appearance** (`showResizeHandles`/`resizeHandleColor`, grid-wide default + per-item override), plus a per-item `resizeHandles` `@Input()` restricting which of the 8 edges/corners actually activate. See [Configurable resize-hint appearance](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/33-resize-hint-appearance).
- **Custom drag-placeholder content** — replace the default plain placeholder box with your own rendered content while dragging. See [Custom drag-placeholder content](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/25-custom-drag-placeholder).
- **`scrollToItem`/`focusItem`**, public methods on `GridLayoutComponent` — programmatically scroll an item into view and/or move keyboard focus to it. See [scrollToItem & focusItem](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/27-scroll-to-item-focus-item).
- **`autoScroll`** — scrolls a container automatically near its edge during drag/resize. See [autoScroll](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/39-auto-scroll).
- **Layout events** — a dedicated example covering the full set of granular drag/lifecycle `@Output()`s together. See [Events](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/03-events).
- **Edit-mode toggle** (`enableEditMode`) — a single grid-wide (or per-item) switch disabling dragging, resizing, and the close button at once. See [Edit mode toggle](https://kdla.winnem.tech/examples/21-edit-mode-toggle).

## Developer experience

- **Full TypeScript support.** Every component, directive, service, and interface is typed and exported from the package's main entry point — see [API](/angular/api/) once that page lands.
- **Minimal runtime dependencies.** The drag/resize engine is built on native Pointer Events, not a third-party library — the same shared engine the Vue and React packages use. Not literally zero beyond Angular/RxJS, though: `package.json`'s own `dependencies` also lists `tslib` (a near-universal, few-KB TypeScript/Angular compiled-output helper), alongside the shared `keystone-dashboard-layout-core`.
- **The same framework-agnostic core** (`keystone-dashboard-layout-core`) Vue and React use for their own grid-layout math (collision detection, movement, compaction, and more) — all three packages share one implementation of the hard, easy-to-get-subtly-wrong parts.
- **Idiomatic Angular.** Standalone components (no `NgModule` required), a DI-scoped `GridEventBusService` instead of Vue's `provide`/`inject` or React's Context, `providedIn: 'root'` services instead of ref-bound composables/hooks, and a marker directive queried via `@ContentChild` instead of a named slot or render prop — the same underlying behavior, expressed the way Angular actually works.
- **Tested end to end, not just at the unit level.** A genuine unit/component test suite (Jest + `jest-preset-angular`) backs every phase, and Stryker mutation testing is configured — see the package's own `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the phase-by-phase history. This package also has a real Playwright e2e suite (11 spec files, 160 tests, all passing across Chromium/Firefox/WebKit), matching Vue and React's own setup — see [Testing philosophy](/angular/guide/project/testing/). The one remaining gap: no dedicated touch-input spec yet, the way the React port has.
- **An editable playground on every example.** "Open in StackBlitz" opens a real, running project seeded from that exact example's own source, in a new tab — not a read-only code snippet.

them:

```ts
  ILayoutItem,
  IGridAriaLabels,
  ICompactor,
  IExportLayoutAsSvgOptions,
} from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-core';
import { ECompactType } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-core';
```

themselves are identical either way — see this package's own reference

GridLayout, GridItem, and two standalone utility components this package exports.

The package exports these from its main entry point:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`GridLayout`](/react/components/grid-layout/props/) | The grid container — owns the layout array, breakpoints, and collision/compaction logic. A fully controlled component (`layout`/`onLayoutChange`). |
| [`GridItem`](/react/components/grid-item/props/) | A single draggable/resizable cell, rendered as a child of `GridLayout`. |
| [`GridItemCloseButton`](/react/components/custom-close-button/) | A standalone close-button building block, for rendering the same affordance somewhere other than `GridItem`'s own built-in close button (e.g. inside a custom header). |
| [`GridItemDragHandle`](/react/components/custom-drag-element/) | A standalone drag-handle building block, for the same reason. |

See [Styling](/react/components/styling/) for the CSS custom properties
and class names used throughout.

```ts
import { GridLayout, GridItem } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-react';
```

There's no default export — always import by name. See [Installation](/react/guide/installation/)
if you haven't added the package yet.

There's also a real, exported close-button component
(`GridItemCloseButton`) and drag-handle component (`GridItemDragHandle`)
— useful when you want those same building blocks rendered somewhere
other than `GridItem`'s own built-in rendering (e.g. inside a custom
header). Most consumers should reach for the simpler, built-in path
first though: a close button is a built-in, per-item opt-in
(`showCloseButton` on `GridLayout`/`ILayoutItem` + an `onItemClose`
callback you handle yourself), and any part of an item is a drag handle
by default — restrict it via `dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom` on the
layout item instead of swapping in a different component.

## The imperative handle

`GridLayout` also exposes an imperative API via `ref` —
`compactNow()`, `duplicateItem(id)`, `undo()`/`redo()`,
`selectItem()`/`clearSelection()`, `alignSelected(edge)`/
`distributeSelected(axis)`, `exportLayoutAsSvg()`, and
`scrollToItem(id)`/`focusItem(id)` — the React equivalent of Vue's own
`defineExpose`'d template-ref methods, reached via `forwardRef`/
`useImperativeHandle` instead. See [Imperative handle](/react/api/interfaces/imperative-handle/)
for the full reference.

## Drag & resize

- **Drag anywhere, or from a handle.** Every item is draggable by default; restrict it to a specific handle with `dragAllowFrom`, or exclude specific elements with `dragIgnoreFrom` (and `resizeIgnoreFrom` for resize specifically). See [Drag allow/ignore elements](/react/examples/drag-allow-ignore-elements/) and [Custom drag handle](/react/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/).
- **Resize from any edge or corner** — top, right, bottom, left, and the diagonals — with optional `preserveAspectRatio` locking. See [Size constraints & aspect ratio](/react/examples/size-constraints-aspect-ratio/), [Restricting resize handles to specific edges](/react/examples/restrict-resize-handles/), and [Resize direction toggles](/react/examples/resize-direction-toggles/).
- **Min/max size constraints** (`minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`) per item. See [Size constraints & aspect ratio](/react/examples/size-constraints-aspect-ratio/).
- **Bounded dragging** (`isBounded`) — keep items from being dragged outside the container. See [Bounded drag](/react/examples/bounded-drag/).
- **Static items** — lock specific items in place; they ignore dragging/resizing entirely and act as fixed obstacles for compaction. See [Static items](/react/examples/static-items/).
- **Per-item `zIndex` override** — pin one item permanently above every other, including while others are mid-resize, regardless of the library's own implicit static/resizing stacking rules. See [Per-item zIndex override](/react/examples/per-item-z-index/).
- **A separate header region** (the `header` render prop on `GridItem`) — an optional header area above an item's own main content, its own scrollable region taking whatever space remains. See [Custom header](/react/examples/custom-header-slot/).
- **Per-item `autoHeight`** — a live-resyncing height, driven by a real `ResizeObserver` on the item's own content rather than a one-time measurement. See [Per-item autoHeight](/react/examples/per-item-auto-height/).
- **`dragActivationDistance`** — a per-pointer-type drag-start threshold, so a small accidental movement doesn't immediately start a drag. See [Drag activation distance](/react/examples/drag-activation-distance/).

## Layout & collision

- **Automatic compaction.** Items fill gaps vertically by default; other items automatically move out of the way of a drag/resize.
- **Pluggable compaction strategy** (`compactType`) — five built-in strategies (vertical, horizontal, none, and overlap variants of each), or replace the algorithm entirely with a custom `compactor` prop. See [Pluggable compaction](/react/examples/pluggable-compaction/).
- **Horizontal shift mode** — push colliding items left/right instead of down. See [Horizontal shift](/react/examples/horizontal-shift/).
- **Prevent collision mode** (`preventCollision`) — block a drag/resize instead of pushing other items, with an `onMoveBlockedByCollision(id)` callback so a consumer can give feedback the moment that happens. See [Prevent collision](/react/examples/prevent-collision/) and [Blocked-move feedback](/react/examples/blocked-move-feedback/).
- **Magnetic snap-to-grid** (`snapToGrid`/`snapThreshold`) — actually adjusts an item's landing position to align with a neighbor, not just a visual guide. See [Snap to grid](/react/examples/snap-to-grid/).
- **Alignment guides** (`showAlignmentGuides`) — Figma-style guide lines while dragging or resizing, wherever an item's edges line up with another's. See [Alignment guides while dragging](/react/examples/alignment-guides/).
- **`restoreOnDrag`** — keep other items from compacting past their pre-drag position while a drag is in progress. See [Layout bounds & rendering options](/react/examples/layout-bounds-rendering-options/).
- **Auto-sizing container** — the grid's height grows/shrinks to fit its content by default (`autoSize`, or the newer `heightMode` prop for finer control including `'scroll'`/`'fit'` modes). See [Auto-size grid on content](/react/examples/auto-size-grid/) and [Height modes](/react/examples/height-modes/).
- **Spacing indicators** (`showSpacingGuides`) — a labeled distance badge (e.g. "2 cols") in the gap between the active item and its nearest neighbor on each side, independently toggleable alongside alignment guides. See [Spacing indicators](/react/examples/spacing-indicators/).
- **Serializable layout.** The `layout` array is a plain, JSON-serializable structure you own — persist it anywhere. See [Save/load layout](/react/examples/save-load-layout/).
- **Named layout presets** (`useLayoutPresets`) — save and switch between multiple named arrangements, layered on the same serialize/restore primitives. See [Named layout presets](/react/examples/named-presets/).
- **Grid-to-SVG export** (`exportLayoutAsSvg()` on the imperative handle) — a dependency-free utility producing a standalone SVG snapshot of the current layout. See [Export layout as SVG](/react/examples/svg-export/).
- **Undo/redo** (`enableUndoRedo`, capped via `undoHistoryLimit`) — opt-in history at committed-change granularity (drag/resize end, add/remove), not per intermediate frame. See [Undo/redo](/react/examples/undo-redo/).
- **Add/remove items freely**, with automatic re-compaction — no manual position math required. See [Add or remove items](/react/examples/add-remove-items/).
- **`distributeEvenly`** — spreads an out-of-bounds item to the next available slot on a responsive breakpoint change, instead of clamping it to the right edge.
- **`compactNow()`/`rearrange()`/`duplicateItem(id)`** on the imperative handle — force an immediate compaction pass, reflow the whole layout, or clone an existing item. See [compactNow, rearrange & duplicateItem](/react/examples/compact-now-rearrange-duplicate-item/).
- **Live layout lifecycle events** (`onLayoutReady`, plus the granular drag/resize callbacks) for observing exactly when the grid settles or an interaction completes. See [Layout lifecycle events](/react/examples/layout-lifecycle-events/).
- **Programmatic grid dimensions** — read/observe the container's own resolved width/columns directly. See [Grid dimensions](/react/examples/grid-dimensions/).
- **Switching layouts, including forcing a full remount** when a `key` change is the simplest way to reset internal state. See [Switching layouts & forcing a remount](/react/examples/switching-layouts-remount/).

## Multi-select & group operations

- **Select multiple items** (`multiSelect`) — click to select, Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+click to add additively, click empty background to clear. See [Multi-select & group move/resize](/react/examples/multi-select-group-move-resize/).
- **Group move and resize** — drag or resize any selected item and the rest of the selection moves or resizes by the same delta, from mouse or keyboard alike. See [Multi-select & group move/resize](/react/examples/multi-select-group-move-resize/).
- **Align/distribute commands** (`alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)` on the imperative handle) — align a selection to an edge, or evenly space what's between. See [Align & distribute selected items](/react/examples/align-distribute-selected/).

## Responsive

- **Breakpoint-based column counts**, with sensible defaults and fully customizable `breakpoints`/`cols`. See [Responsive breakpoints](/react/examples/responsive-breakpoints/).
- **Pre-defined layouts per breakpoint** (`responsiveLayouts`), for full control over how content reflows instead of relying on auto-generation. See [Responsive predefined layouts](/react/examples/responsive-predefined-layouts/).

## Internationalization

- **RTL mirroring** (`isMirrored`) for an entire layout or individual items (per-item opt-out via `ILayoutItem.isMirrored`) — positions (and dragging) flip horizontally with a single prop. See [Mirrored (RTL)](/react/examples/mirrored-rtl/).

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard move & resize.** Every non-static, editable item is keyboard-focusable — arrow keys move it, Shift+arrow keys resize it — without needing any extra configuration, including RTL-aware key direction and `multiSelect` group-move/resize engagement. See [Accessibility scope](/react/guide/project/accessibility/) for the full scope, including what's deliberately not (yet) covered.
- **Screen reader support** — interactive items are announced with an item-role description and a description of the available keyboard controls; visible focus indicator for keyboard users.
- **Localizable ARIA strings** (`ariaLabels`) — the close button's label, role description, and the keyboard move/resize instructions are overridable (`GridLayout` grid-wide default, `GridItem` per-item override), rather than hardcoded English literals. See [Localizable ARIA strings](/react/examples/aria-labels/).

## Cross-grid & external drag-and-drop

- **Drag items from outside the grid** (`allowOutsideDrop`) using the browser's native HTML5 drag-and-drop API, with a live drop-position placeholder while dragging over the grid. See [Drag, drop from outside](/react/examples/outside-drag-drop/) and [outsideDropAccept & readOutsideDropPayload](/react/examples/outside-drop-accept-payload/).
- **Drag items between two independent grids** (`allowCrossGridDrag`/`disableExternalDrop`/`layoutId`) via a real first-fit bin-pack, not a naive placement then compaction sorts out. See [Drag, drop from grid to grid](/react/examples/cross-grid-drag-drop/) and [Cross-grid drop restrictions](/react/examples/cross-grid-drop-restrictions/).
- **Multiple grids on one page** with zero shared state or configuration beyond an optional `layoutId`. See [Multiple grids](/react/examples/multiple-grids/) and [Drag, drop from outside into multiple grids](/react/examples/outside-drag-drop-multiple-grids/).

## Styling & customization

- **Unstyled-by-default content** — `GridItem`'s children hold whatever you put there; the library only handles position/size.
- **Built-in close button** (`showCloseButton` + an `onItemClose` callback you handle yourself), or bring your own via the exported [`GridItemCloseButton`](/react/components/custom-close-button/)/[`GridItemDragHandle`](/react/components/custom-drag-element/) components. Any part of an item is a drag handle by default, restrictable via `dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom`. See [Show close button](/react/examples/close-button/) and [Custom drag handle & close button](/react/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/).
- **Configurable border radius** per item (`borderRadiusPx`/`useBorderRadius`, grid-wide default + per-item override). See [Border radius](/react/examples/border-radius/).
- **Optional grid line guides** (`showGridLines`), useful while building a layout or as a permanent visual aid. See [Show grid lines](/react/examples/grid-lines/).
- **Configurable transition duration/easing** (`transitionDurationMs`/`transitionTimingFunction`), applied via CSS custom properties. See [Configurable transition duration & easing](/react/examples/transition-duration-easing/).
- **Custom drag-placeholder content** — replace the default plain placeholder box with your own rendered content while dragging. See [Custom drag-placeholder content](/react/examples/custom-drag-placeholder/).
- **`scrollToItem`/`focusItem`** on the imperative handle — programmatically scroll an item into view and/or move keyboard focus to it. See [scrollToItem & focusItem](/react/examples/scroll-to-item-focus-item/).
- **`autoScroll`** — scrolls a container automatically near its edge during drag/resize. See [autoScroll](/react/examples/auto-scroll/).
- **Layout events** — a dedicated example covering the full set of granular drag/lifecycle callbacks together. See [Events](/react/examples/events/).
- **Edit-mode toggle** (`enableEditMode`) — a single grid-wide (or per-item) switch disabling dragging, resizing, and the close button at once. See [Edit mode toggle](/react/examples/edit-mode-toggle/).

## Developer experience

- **Full TypeScript support.** Every prop, callback, and interface is typed and exported from the package's main entry point — see [API](/react/api/) once that page lands.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** The drag/resize engine is built on native Pointer Events, not a third-party library — the same shared engine the Vue package uses.
- **The same framework-agnostic core** (`keystone-dashboard-layout-core`) Vue uses for its own grid-layout math (collision detection, movement, compaction, and more) — both packages share one implementation of the hard, easy-to-get-subtly-wrong parts.
- **Idiomatic React.** A fully controlled component (`layout`/`onLayoutChange`), hooks instead of composables, Context instead of `provide`/`inject`, render props instead of named slots, and a `ref`-based imperative handle instead of `defineExpose` — the same underlying behavior, expressed the way React actually works.
- **Well-tested.** A real unit, mutation, and end-to-end test suite backs the package — see the package's own `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the phase-by-phase history.
- **An editable playground on every example.** "Open in StackBlitz" opens a real, running project seeded from that exact example's own source, in a new tab — not a read-only code snippet.

The exact close button GridItem renders internally for showCloseButton — exported for standalone reuse.

The default close button rendered inside a `GridItem` when
`showCloseButton` is true. Also exported standalone from the package's
main entry point, in case you want to render the same button somewhere
else (a custom header, say) and wire it to the same removal event
yourself.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { CustomCloseButton } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-vue';

function removeItem(id: string | number): void {
  layout.value = layout.value.filter((item) => item.i !== id);
}
</script>

<template>
  <CustomCloseButton :i="item.i" @remove-grid-item="removeItem" />
</template>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `i` | `string \| number` | `-1` | The id of the `GridItem` this button removes when clicked. `-1` is treated as a "no item" sentinel — clicking with the default value is a no-op, rather than emitting a removal for a nonexistent item. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `remove-grid-item` | `(i: string \| number)` | The button was clicked with a real `i` set (not the `-1` default). |

:::note[Payload type isn't compile-time checked]
The payload shown above is accurate for what's actually emitted, but
this component's own emit declaration doesn't statically type the
payload argument — only the event *name* is checked by TypeScript, not
your handler's parameter type.
:::

## Why you'd use this instead of `showCloseButton`

`showCloseButton` is the right choice for the common case — the built-in
button, styled via the classes documented in
[Styling → GridItem](/vue/components/styling/css-grid-item/). Reach for
`CustomCloseButton` directly when you want the exact same click/removal
behavior but need to place it somewhere `GridItem`'s own internal
rendering doesn't reach — inside a custom header slot, for instance. See
[Custom drag handle & close button](/vue/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/)
for a full working example using both `CustomCloseButton` and
`CustomDragElement` together.
A standalone drag-handle widget, not used internally by the library — pair it with GridItem's dragAllowFrom prop.

A small drag-handle widget, exported for placing inside a `GridItem`'s
slot content when you want dragging restricted to a single handle rather
than the whole item — pair it with `GridItem`'s `dragAllowFrom` prop so
only this element starts a drag.

:::caution[The grab target is a small circle, not the visible button]
The rendered markup is a labeled `<button>` **plus a separate**, small
decorative circle element carrying the `vue-draggable-handle` class —
confirmed directly from the component's own template. `dragAllowFrom`
matches that circle specifically, not the button/text you actually see
labeled. Clicking the visible text does **not** start a drag; only the
small circle (rendered at the widget's own bottom-right corner) does.
:::

Not used anywhere internally in this library — a standalone, opt-in
utility component, exported from the package's main entry point
alongside `CustomCloseButton`.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { CustomDragElement } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-vue';
</script>

<template>
  <GridItem drag-allow-from=".vue-draggable-handle" :h="item.h" :i="item.i" :w="item.w" :x="item.x" :y="item.y">
    <CustomDragElement text="⠿" />
    Item content
  </GridItem>
</template>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | `'x'` | Label rendered inside the handle's own button. |

## Pairing with `resizeIgnoreFrom`

If the handle sits near a corner, it can land inside the same
edge-proximity margin the resize engine already uses to detect a resize
gesture — meaning grabbing the handle could start a resize instead of
the drag `dragAllowFrom` was meant to restrict things to. Excluding the
handle from `resizeIgnoreFrom` as well is what actually stops the two
from fighting over the same gesture:

```vue
<GridItem
  drag-allow-from=".vue-draggable-handle"
  resize-ignore-from=".vue-draggable-handle"
  ...>
```

See [Custom drag handle & close button](/vue/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/)
for a full working example combining this with `CustomCloseButton`.
A real first-fit bin-pack — removing an item from the middle of the grid opens a gap the next added item actually reuses.

import AddRemoveItems from '../../../../components/examples/10-add-remove-items.vue';
import AddRemoveItemsSource from '../../../../components/examples/10-add-remove-items.vue?raw';
import ExampleTryIt from '../../../../components/harness/ExampleTryIt.astro';

<ExampleTryIt code={AddRemoveItemsSource} filename="add-remove-items.vue" playground>
  <AddRemoveItems client:visible />
</ExampleTryIt>

Where a newly-added item actually lands is entirely up to the
consumer — the library only places it wherever `x`/`y` say to, then
compacts around it. Appending with `x:0, y:0` (or `y: Infinity`,
placed at the very bottom instead) and letting compaction settle it is
the simplest convention, but it never *reuses a gap* left by a removed
item — a new item always lands in a fresh row even when there's
clearly room higher up.

This demo's own `addItem` does a real first-fit bin-pack instead, via
this package's own exported `findFirstFitSlot`: remove an item from
the middle of the grid, then add a new one, and it lands in the gap
left behind. The toggle demonstrates a second placement strategy —
appending to the end of the first row specifically, falling back to
the general bin-pack once that row is full.

The two strategies only produce a *visibly different* result once
there's an actual gap for them to disagree about — on a fresh, packed
layout, both fill the first row left-to-right and wrap to a new row
the same way, so toggling it on or off looks identical. To see the
difference: remove item `1` (opening a gap at `x:3`), leave the toggle
on, then add an item — it skips that gap and lands past the row's own
rightmost occupied edge instead, rather than filling it the way the
general bin-pack would.

`.filter()` the same way as above.

Both are exposed on the `GridLayout` instance, only meaningful with
`multiSelect` on. `alignSelected` treats the **first-selected item**
(insertion order, not an arbitrary one) as the anchor — it never moves;
every other selected item aligns to its edge or center. Needs at least

actual position, not selection order) stay exactly where they are, and
only what's "in between" spaces out evenly across the span those two

land an item on top of a *non-selected* item is skipped for that one
item; landing on another item that's *also* part of the same
align/distribute batch isn't treated as a collision at all, since
that's frequently the whole point of the command.

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `'auto'` (default when unset) | Grows/shrinks to fit content — same as the older `autoSize: true`. In the demo above, this deliberately overflows the dashed frame, since nothing here constrains it. |
| `'fixed'` | No explicit height applied at all — the consumer's own CSS decides. Same as `autoSize: false`. |
| `'scroll'` | Same as `'fixed'`, but also applies an inline `overflow-y: auto`, so content taller than whatever height your own CSS gives it scrolls internally instead of overflowing. |
| `'fit'` | Height locked to `100%` of the parent container, with the same `overflow-y: auto` as `'scroll'` — for a grid meant to fill a fixed-size panel exactly. |

behavior change for existing consumers who only use `autoSize`.

```ts

gridRef.value.toggleItemSelection('b');  // toggles 'b' in/out

```

## Multi-select

Off by default (`multiSelect: false`) — every prior behavior is
completely unaffected when this stays off. When on:

- **Click** an item — selects only it, replacing any prior selection.
- **Shift+click or Ctrl/Cmd+click** — adds/removes that item from the
  current selection additively.
- **Click empty grid background** — clears the selection entirely.

Dragging or resizing any *selected* item while more than one item is
selected moves/resizes every other selected item by the same delta —
also works from the keyboard (arrow keys/Shift+arrow on a focused,
selected item), not just mouse/touch drag.

A passenger that's static, or has `isDraggable`/`isResizable`
explicitly `false`, never moves or resizes as part of a group gesture
— the same guarantee a static item already has against the normal
collision-push cascade. A passenger's own `minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`
are also respected individually during group resize, not just clamped
to the anchor's own limits (or a bare floor of 1) — see item "d" in the
demo above, which stops at its own `maxW` of 3 even while the other,
unconstrained items keep growing.

:::caution[Deliberately scoped, not fully collision-aware]
The delta is applied directly to every other selected item's position
or size — there's no per-passenger collision detection against
*non-selected* items during the gesture itself, only the
dragged/resized item gets the usual collision/bounds handling.
Compaction (per `compactType`) still runs normally once the
gesture ends.
:::

Listen for `@selection-changed` (payload: the full current selection as
an array) to react to selection changes, or read the exposed
`selectedItems` directly.

A named, scoped slot on `GridItem` — receives `{ edge }` (`'n'`, `'s'`,
`'e'`, `'w'`, `'ne'`, `'nw'`, `'se'`, `'sw'`), letting you render
different content per edge/corner if you want. Renders inside the same
small hit-area `showResizeHandles`/`resizeHandleColor` already use for
the color/visibility toggle — both can be combined, or the slot used on
its own for a fully custom icon instead of a plain colored dot.

:::note[Why this one starts inside a fixed-height frame]
`layout` starts empty, and `GridLayout`'s own `autoSize` (default
`true`) sizes the container to fit its content — with zero items, that
collapses to almost nothing, leaving no visible area to drop onto at
all. `height-mode="fit"` inside a `.drop-zone-frame` with a real CSS
`height` fixes this: the grid fills that frame regardless of how many
items it currently holds, so there's always a genuine drop target.
:::

:::caution[A real gotcha with native drag-and-drop]
`dataTransfer.getData()` only returns real values during the `drop`
event itself — during `dragenter`/`dragover` (when `outsideDropAccept`
is actually called) it always returns an empty string, regardless of
what the source set. This is a genuine, confirmed bug this example
had at first: `outsideDropAccept` tried to parse the full JSON payload
to check its `kind` field, which silently rejected every drag — real
widget or not — since the payload was never readable at that point.
The browser showed a "not a valid drop target" cursor and the drop
never fired.

The fix: only `dataTransfer.types` (the list of MIME types present,
not their values) is reliably readable during `dragenter`/`dragover`.
This example's drag source now sets a second, value-less MIME type
(`'application/x-widget'`) only on the real widget, and
`outsideDropAccept` checks `dataTransfer.types.includes('application/x-widget')`
instead of trying to read the actual payload. The full JSON payload is
still read via `readOutsideDropPayload` — just at `drop` time, in
`@item-dropped-from-outside`, where `.getData()` genuinely works.
:::

See [Drag, drop from outside](/vue/examples/outside-drag-drop/) for
`allowOutsideDrop` itself, and [API → Overview](/vue/api/) for where
`readOutsideDropPayload` is exported from.

Distinct from [Configurable resize-hint appearance](/vue/examples/resize-hint-appearance/)

`snapThreshold` is how close, in grid units, a dragged item's edge needs
to be to another item's edge before it snaps — default `1`. Unlike
[alignment guides](/vue/examples/alignment-guides/) (`showAlignmentGuides`,
purely visual), this actually changes where the item lands: once the
pointer's dragged-to position is within threshold of an edge alignment,
the position adjusts to match it exactly, both in the live placeholder
while dragging and in the final committed position on drop.

exactly where the magnetic snap is about to lock to.

### v2.0.0 — 2026-07-14

The first major release. Two large passes: the first brought cross-grid
and outside-the-grid drag-and-drop, a full test/CI/docs foundation, and
this documentation site; the second closed out the rest of the
then-current roadmap in one batch — magnetic snapping, layout tools,
persistence presets, export, and localization — plus a further round of
e2e coverage and a bug found while writing it.

**Added (first pass):** cross-grid drag/drop
(`allowCrossGridDrag`/`disableExternalDrop` — see
[Drag, drop from grid to grid](/vue/examples/cross-grid-drag-drop/)); native
drag-and-drop from outside the grid system entirely
(`allowOutsideDrop`/`outsideDropWidth`/`outsideDropHeight` — see
[Drag, drop from outside](/vue/examples/outside-drag-drop/) and
[into multiple grids](/vue/examples/outside-drag-drop-multiple-grids/)); resize from **all four
edges and their corners** with cursor affordance; full unit/component/e2e
test suite (**98%+ coverage**, enforced in CI); CI/CD across Node 18/20/22 with a
bundle-size regression check, dependency audit, and automated releases;
keyboard move/resize accessibility support; a `demo/` app and a restyled
`sandbox/` test bench; a live layout viewer under every example.

**Added (second pass):** `compactNow()`/`rearrange()` (on-demand
compaction); collision-safe `duplicateItem(id)`; a

[Blocked-move feedback](/vue/examples/blocked-move-feedback/); per-item `autoHeight`

`outsideDropAccept` and a typed outside-drop payload helper

**Fixed:** 40+ source-level bugs found while building tests, adding
features, and writing documentation in the first pass — several
crash-level, several silent (changing `margin`/`showCloseButton`/RTL

`undo()`/`redo()`/`canUndo`/`canRedo` are all exposed on the `GridLayout`
instance, the same `ref`-based pattern as `compactNow()`/`scrollToItem()`.
A snapshot is captured at the *start* of a drag/resize and committed at
its *end* — not per intermediate frame — so one undo reverts a whole
gesture at once, not one step per pixel moved. `undoHistoryLimit`
(default `50`) caps how many snapshots `undo()` can step back through.
What Keystone Dashboard Layout for Vue is, what you get, and where to go next.

Keystone Dashboard Layout for Vue is a Vue 3 component library for building
draggable, resizable, responsive dashboard grids — the kind of UI you'd
use for a customizable analytics dashboard, a widget board, or any screen
where users rearrange content themselves.

It's a TypeScript-first library built from the ground up on Vue 3's
Composition API, using a native, Pointer Events-based drag/resize engine
with no third-party runtime dependency for it at all.

## What you get

- **`GridLayout`** — the container. Owns the layout array (position/size
  of every item), responsive breakpoint state, and collision/compaction
  logic.
- **`GridItem`** — a single draggable/resizable cell, rendered inside
  `GridLayout`'s default slot. You control what's inside it — text,
  images, charts, forms, anything.
- **Two small utility components** — `CustomCloseButton` and
  `CustomDragElement` — exported in case you want to reuse the library's
  own default close button or build a dedicated drag handle.

## How it fits together

```vue
<GridLayout v-model:layout="layout">
  <GridItem v-for="item in layout" :key="item.i" v-bind="item">
    <!-- your content -->
  </GridItem>
</GridLayout>
```

`layout` is a plain array of `{ i, x, y, w, h, ... }` objects — one per
`GridItem`. You own that array; the library reads and updates it as the
user drags and resizes things. Everything else (collision resolution,
compaction, responsive breakpoint switching) happens automatically based
on the props you set.

## Where to go next

- [Installation](/vue/guide/installation/) — add the package to your project.
- [Examples](/vue/examples/) — interactive, copy-pasteable examples, from a
  basic grid to responsive breakpoints and drag-drop between grids.
- [Components](/vue/components/) — full prop/event/slot reference for `GridLayout` and `GridItem`.
- [API](/vue/api/) — exported TypeScript types, interfaces, and enums.

## Design goals

A few decisions that shape how the library behaves, worth knowing up
front:

- **You own the data.** The layout array is yours — the library mutates
  it in place / emits updates, but never hides state you can't inspect or
  serialize (see [v-model & save/load layout](/vue/examples/save-load-layout/)).
- **Sensible defaults, explicit overrides.** Most behavior (draggable,
  resizable, bounded, etc.) can be set once on `GridLayout` and inherited
  by every item, or overridden per-item when needed.
- **Composition over configuration objects.** Props map directly to
  documented, individually-typed options rather than one large opaque
  config object — better autocomplete, better documentation per option.

Most prop names carry over unchanged — the two libraries share a

| `rowHeight` | `rowHeight` | Same. |
| `margin` | `margin` | Same `[x, y]` pixel tuple. |
| `isDraggable` | `isDraggable` | Same — grid-wide default, per-item overridable. |
| `isResizable` | `isResizable` | Same. |
| `isBounded` | `isBounded` | Same. |
| `isMirrored` | `isMirrored` | Same — RTL mirroring. |

| `useStyleCursor` | *(no equivalent)* | Cursor styling isn't independently toggleable here. |

Three event names carry over exactly: **`layout-updated`**,
**`layout-ready`**, and **`breakpoint-changed`** all fire with the same
name and a compatible payload shape. `move`/`moved`/`resize`/`resized`

## Behavioral differences

- **Compaction is a pluggable strategy, not a boolean.** `verticalCompact:
  false` doesn't map to a different boolean here — it maps to
  `compactType: ECompactType.NONE`. `verticalCompact: true` (the
  original's default) maps to this library's own default,
  `ECompactType.VERTICAL`. This library additionally supports
  `HORIZONTAL`, `VERTICAL_OVERLAP`, and `HORIZONTAL_OVERLAP`, and a
  fully custom `compactor` — see
  [Pluggable compaction](/vue/examples/pluggable-compaction/).
- **No `dragOption`/`resizeOption` passthrough.** The original libraries
  wrap `interactjs` and expose its own options object directly. This
  library uses its own native Pointer Events drag/resize engine with no
  underlying third-party library to configure — most of what
  `dragOption`/`resizeOption` were used for in practice (activation
  distance, specific resize handles, aspect-ratio locking) has a direct,
  typed prop instead: `dragActivationDistance`, `resizeHandles`,
  `preserveAspectRatio`.
- **Five extra responsive breakpoints by default.** If your layout
  logic (or CSS) assumes exactly `lg`/`md`/`sm`/`xs`/`xxs`, pass explicit
  `breakpoints`/`cols` objects rather than relying on this library's
  wider 7-tier default.
Fixes for the most common real failure modes when integrating GridLayout for Vue — grid stuck at zero width, dragging not starting, breakpoints not switching, and layout validation errors.

## The grid renders with zero width, or collapses to nothing

`GridLayout` measures its own root element's `offsetWidth` via a
`ResizeObserver`, and only updates its internal width `if (offsetWidth >
0)` — a guard against the well-known case where `offsetWidth` reads `0`
while an element (or one of its ancestors) has `display: none`, is
`v-if`-false, or hasn't been laid out yet. When that guard fails, the
grid doesn't error — it silently keeps whatever width it last measured
(or never measures at all), which looks like a frozen or collapsed
layout with no console output to explain why.

Most common causes:

- Rendering `GridLayout` inside a `v-if`-gated tab/panel/modal that
  starts hidden. Prefer `v-show` (keeps the element in the layout tree,
  just visually hidden — width becomes measurable the instant it's
  shown) over `v-if` for anything containing a grid, or force a
  re-measure (e.g. `nextTick` + a resize-triggering change) right after
  the panel becomes visible.
- A flex/grid parent that hasn't completed its own layout pass on the
  same tick the grid mounts. Give the grid's parent container an
  explicit width or `min-width` rather than relying on content-driven
  sizing.
- The container has no defined height and depends on the grid's own
  content to size it, while the grid depends on the container for
  width — a sizing cycle that resolves to zero either way.

## Dragging doesn't start on some (or all) items

If a `GridItem` sets `dragAllowFrom`, that selector is checked
**first, and exclusively** — a pointer-down target that doesn't match
it is rejected outright, and `dragIgnoreFrom` never even gets
evaluated. A `dragAllowFrom` selector that doesn't match anything on
that item (a typo, or markup that changed after the selector was
written) silently disables dragging for the whole item — there's no
warning, since from the library's perspective this is working as
configured.

Check, in order:

1. Is `dragAllowFrom` set on this item? If so, does the selector
   actually match an element that exists inside it right now?
2. Is `isDraggable` `false` on this specific item, overriding the
   grid-wide default?
3. Is the grid-wide `isDraggable` prop itself `false`?

## Responsive breakpoints don't switch when I expect them to

Breakpoint resolution is driven by the grid **container's own measured
width** (the same `ResizeObserver`-sourced value from the section
above) — never `window.innerWidth`. This is deliberate and correct for
grids embedded in a sidebar, iframe, or any container narrower than the
viewport, but it means the zero-width failure mode above has a second
symptom: if the container never gets a real measured width, breakpoint
switching doesn't run either, since it's derived from the same stuck
value.

## Server-side rendering (Nuxt / SSR)

The `GridLayout` component itself has no explicit SSR guard, but it
also doesn't need one: the `ResizeObserver` and pointer-event listeners
are only ever created inside `onMounted`, which Vue's own SSR contract
guarantees does not run during server rendering. The pieces that *do*
carry explicit `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guards are the
optional layout-persistence and layout-preset composables
(`useLayoutStorage`, `useLayoutPresets`) — safe to call during SSR,
they simply no-op until the client takes over.

## `Invalid parameter ...` / `Layout is not valid` errors

These come from the core validators (`layoutValidator`,
`keysValidator`, `marginValidator`, `breakpointsValidator`) rejecting
malformed input before it reaches the rendering/collision logic. The
message names the actual problem — a few worth knowing up front rather
than debugging from the message alone:

- **`Layout can not be empty`** — an empty array was passed as the
  initial `layout`; render nothing (or a placeholder) until you have at
  least one item, rather than passing `[]`.
  - **`Layout is not valid`** / **`Invalid parameter layoutItem id
  passed`** — every item needs a unique, stable `i`; duplicate or
  missing ids fail here.
- **`Invalid parameter cols passed`** / **`Parameter cols must be
  greater than 0`** — `colNum` (or a responsive breakpoint's own column
  count) resolved to `0` or a non-number, usually from a computed value
  that hasn't initialized yet.
- **`Invalid parameter marginPx passed`** — `margin` expects a `[x, y]`
  pixel tuple, not a CSS string like `"8px"`.

What Keystone Dashboard Layout for Angular is, what you get, and where to go next.

Keystone Dashboard Layout for Angular is an Angular component library for
building draggable, resizable, responsive dashboard grids — the kind of
UI you'd use for a customizable analytics dashboard, a widget board, or
any screen where users rearrange content themselves.

It's a TypeScript-first library built on the exact same shared
`keystone-dashboard-layout-core` algorithms and native, Pointer
Events-based drag/resize engine the Vue and React packages use — all
three frameworks share one implementation of the hard, easy-to-get-
subtly-wrong parts (collision, compaction, responsive breakpoint math)
rather than each maintaining their own copy. Angular has reached full
feature parity with both.

## What you get

- **`GridLayoutComponent`** (selector `kdl-grid-layout`) — the
  container. A **fully controlled** component: it never mutates the
  `layout` array (or any item in it) you pass in — every drag/resize
  tick (and the compaction that follows it) is reported via a
  `layoutChange` `@Output()` with a brand-new array. The same
  controlled-data-flow contract the React package uses, rather than
  Vue's own two-way `v-model:layout` binding.
- **`GridItemComponent`** (selector `kdl-grid-item`) — a single
  draggable/resizable cell. Unlike the React package, position and
  size are this component's **own direct `@Input()`s** (`i`/`x`/`y`/
  `w`/`h`, all required) rather than fields read off a matching layout
  item — you bind each one explicitly in your own template's `@for`
  loop, the same shape Vue's own `GridItem` uses.
- **Public imperative methods on `GridLayoutComponent`** — reached via
  a template reference variable (`#grid` + `@ViewChild`), the Angular
  equivalent of Vue's `defineExpose`'d template-ref methods or React's
  `ref`-based imperative handle: `compactNow()`, `rearrange()`,
  `duplicateItem(id)`, `undo()`/`redo()`, `selectItem()`/
  `clearSelection()`, `alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)`,
  `exportLayoutAsSvg()`, `scrollToItem(id)`/`focusItem(id)`, and more.
- **`GridLayoutStorageService`** and **`GridLayoutPresetsService`**
  (both `providedIn: 'root'`) — injectable services wrapping layout
  persistence (serializing to/from `localStorage`) and named layout
  presets. Unlike Vue's ref-bound composables, every method here
  takes/returns a plain layout value directly — you call `save()`/
  `load()` from wherever you already own your own `layout` state.
- **`GridItemHeaderDirective`** — a marker directive
  (`[kdlGridItemHeader]`) applied to your own header content, letting
  `GridItemComponent` project it into a dedicated header region instead
  of its plain default content.

There's also a real, exported close-button component
(`GridItemCloseButtonComponent`) and drag-handle component
(`GridItemDragHandleComponent`), matching Vue and React — useful when
you want those same building blocks rendered somewhere other than
`GridItemComponent`'s own built-in rendering (e.g. inside a custom
header). Most consumers should reach for the simpler, built-in path
first though: a close button is a built-in, per-item opt-in
(`showCloseButton` + a `removeItem` `@Output()` you handle yourself),
and any part of an item is a drag handle by default, restrictable via
`dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom`.

## How it fits together

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-angular';
import type { TLayout } from 'keystone-dashboard-layout-core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dashboard',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent],
  template: `
    <kdl-grid-layout [layout]="layout" (layoutChange)="layout = $event">
      @for (item of layout; track item.i) {
        <kdl-grid-item [i]="item.i" [x]="item.x" [y]="item.y" [w]="item.w" [h]="item.h">
          Item {{ item.i }}
        </kdl-grid-item>
      }
    </kdl-grid-layout>
  `,
})
export class DashboardComponent {
  layout: TLayout = [
    { i: 'a', x: 0, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
    { i: 'b', x: 2, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
  ];
}
```

`layout` is a plain array of `{ i, x, y, w, h, ... }` objects. You own
that array; `layoutChange` hands you a new one every time the user
drags or resizes something, and you decide what to do with it (usually
just reassigning your own field, as above). `GridItemComponent` itself
still needs `x`/`y`/`w`/`h` bound explicitly per item — this component
doesn't read them off `layout` automatically the way React's `GridItem`
does. Everything else (collision resolution, compaction, responsive
breakpoint switching) happens automatically based on the props you set
on `GridLayoutComponent`.

## Design goals

A few decisions that shape how the library behaves, worth knowing up
front:

- **You own the data.** `layout` is a plain, serializable array you
  control — the library never mutates it in place, only ever hands you
  a new one via `layoutChange`.
- **Sensible defaults, explicit overrides.** Most behavior (draggable,
  resizable, bounded, etc.) can be set once on `GridLayoutComponent`
  and inherited by every item via a DI-scoped event bus, or overridden
  per-item when needed.
- **Idiomatic Angular, not a literal Vue-to-Angular transliteration.**
  Vue's `provide`/`inject` eventBus becomes an injectable,
  component-scoped `GridEventBusService`; its composables become
  `providedIn: 'root'` services; its named slots become a marker
  directive (`GridItemHeaderDirective`) queried via `@ContentChild`;
  and its reactive two-way binding becomes the standard `@Input()`/
  `@Output()` pattern — the same underlying behavior, expressed the
  way Angular actually works.
